newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: LME ALUMINIUM SEEN RISING, COPPER RANGE-TRADING.
newsitem.headline: LME ALUMINIUM SEEN RISING, COPPER RANGE-TRADING.

text.p: Aluminium prices on the London Metal Exchange (LME) are seen rising further later on Friday due to a speculative squeeze, although there are also increasing expectations a sharp correction is likely soon, dealers said.
"There's no relief in sight. I would not exclude seeing US$1,800 on the charts. But once sentiment turns around, the market will go down faster than it went up," a dealer said.
"Technically, ally (aluminium) is overbought. There may be a slight pullback, but a lot of clients are looking for an opportunity to buy into it," a senior dealer added.
Three-month aluminium hit a 22-month peak in London on Thursday of $1,775 a tonne before shedding its gains to be indicated late on the day at $1,755/58 a tonne.
The metal was quoted at $1,750/55 at 0205 GMT in Asia.
A Japanese dealer said mild profit-taking today should trim another $20-$30 from the aluminium price.

But broker Rudolf Wolff said in its daily review that the metal's "strong close and the technical indicators extending up suggests further challenges of overhead resistance, placed at $1,786 and then $1,805."
Copper prices, on the other hand, are expected to trade in a range with an upward bias, dealers said.
"It looks pretty well-supported although it may struggle on the upside," a dealer said, adding the red metal will run into good selling if it approaches the $2,350 a tonne level.
Three-month copper was indicated at $2,325/30 a tonne at 0200 GMT on Friday against the late quote on the LME on Thursday of $2,326/29.
"I thought copper was going to fall further and come down to around $2,300. But it should range-trade for now and I don't believe it will dip below $2,300," a trader said.
A Japanese trader said copper should go up slightly on Friday while Rudolf Wolff expects the red metal to show further strength "with challenges of $2,338 and then $2,386."
LME zinc prices also look firm with ample forward buying helping to push prices higher.
"I think zinc should still go up," a dealer said.
LME zinc was quoted at around $1,535/40 a tonne at 0200 GMT from the kerb close on Thursday of $1,540.
